'''Thearterra''' was an obscure<ref name="TEA" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="DJ">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey]]''</ref> located in the [[S-K system]] of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]' [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Space]]. A [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] linked the world to the [[Avidich system/Legends|Avidich system]]. The surface of Thearterra was constantly racked by [[Volcano/Legends|volcanoes]], [[Water/Legends|hailstorms]], and [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]]. The world was part of the [[Chiss]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]' government of the Chiss Ascendancy.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|There has been a lot of contradictory information published about the Chiss over the years, so I pray that this section is relatively error-free. There's also an Easter Egg in here, but I'm not saying what it is.|[[Daniel Wallace]]|<ref name="SW Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|147|Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 5 of 5)}}</ref>}}
Thearterra was first mentioned in the [[2002]] novel ''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey]]'', written by [[Elaine Cunningham]].<ref name="DJ" /> The planet was first identified as Thearterra in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', written by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]]. The book refers to it as "an obscure body in the S-K system,"<ref name="TEA" /> which are the exact words used by General Klytus to describe [[Earth/Legends|Earth]] to Ming the Merciless in the opening scenes of the [[1980]] film [[Wikipedia:Flash Gordon (film)|''Flash Gordon'']] Additionally, the description of the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] climate matches that of planetary attacks that Ming inflicts upon the Earth in the movie.<ref name="FG">{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Flash Gordon (film)|''Flash Gordon'']]|director=[[Wikipedia:Mike Hodges|Mike Hodges]]|prod=Starling Productions|year=[[1980]]}}</ref>
